_comment: The Basement cases (CP7). Original fiction. evidence.kind: key (supports a question's best answer) | support | red_herring | unreliable (players are not told). 'sensitive' cards are flagged privately on the holder's phone. questions[].credit = partial credit per option. tone is hidden from players.

items.title: WHAT HAPPENED IN THE BASEMENT?
items.setup: A child's birthday party was being prepared in the studio basement. At 6pm the cake was found destroyed. The door was locked all afternoon.

evidence.text: A small window near the ceiling is open. The latch was opened from the inside, days ago, for the damp.
There are small muddy prints across the table. Four toes each. Very neat.
Only the icing and the sponge are gone. The candles have been carefully left in a pile.
The bins outside have been knocked over every night this week.
There is a long reddish hair caught on the window frame.
Neil had the only key to the basement. He was in the canteen all afternoon. Several witnesses.
The birthday boy's uncle 'hates cake' and 'hates that boy'.
A faint smell of wet dog. Or something like a dog.
The party bags are untouched. The cash box beside them is untouched.
Graham's dressing room is directly above. He says he heard 'a sort of yap'.

investigations.label: CHECK THE WINDOW
investigations.text: The gap is just big enough for something the size of a medium dog. There are claw marks on the sill.

investigations.label: SMELL THE CAKE PLATE
investigations.text: Icing, mud, and something musky and wild. Not a person.

investigations.label: ASK THE CARETAKER
investigations.text: 'We've had a fox in the bins all week. Cheeky thing. Ginger.'

items.reveal: A fox came in through the open basement window, ate the cake, and left the candles in a neat pile. It has done this before.

items.title: WHAT HAPPENED TO THE TRIFLE?
items.setup: The Christmas trifle in the staff kitchenette was found with a deep hand-sized hole in it, and the floor was wet. Three people had access.

evidence.text: The hole in the trifle has finger marks. Five fingers. Small hands.
The wet patch on the floor runs from the fridge to the sink, not from the door.
The fridge has been leaking since Tuesday. A bucket under it is full.
Carol from make-up wears a large ring. There is no ring mark in the custard.
Somebody has washed one spoon and put it back, still wet.
The runner, Danny, was seen licking his fingers at 3pm. He says it was jam.
Neil is on a diet and has been 'very honest about it'.
There is custard on the handle of the tea urn.
The trifle was labelled 'DO NOT. CAROL.'
Danny wears a size small glove. The hole is the size of a small hand.

investigations.label: CHECK THE BIN
investigations.text: A jam doughnut wrapper. Unopened. So it wasn't jam.

investigations.label: LOOK UNDER THE FRIDGE
investigations.text: The leak is real, and it's a lot of water. The wet floor is the fridge's fault, not a culprit's.

investigations.label: CHECK THE URN
investigations.text: Custard fingerprints on the urn. Small ones. Someone made a cup of tea after.

questions.ask: WHO PUT THEIR HAND IN THE TRIFLE?

items.reveal: Danny the runner put his whole hand in the trifle, washed one spoon in a panic and made himself a cup of tea. The wet floor was just the fridge.
items.graham_reveal: Danny's been let go. Not for this. For other reasons. But also for this.

items.title: WHO EMPTIED THE PROP STORE?
items.setup: Overnight, every rubber chicken in the prop store disappeared. Forty-one of them. The alarm did not go off.

evidence.text: The alarm log shows it was switched off at 01:12 with the correct code.
Only four people know the alarm code: Neil, Carol, Graham and the night guard.
The night guard's van was seen leaving at 01:30, riding very low.
A market stall in town is selling 'vintage TV chickens' this morning.
Graham says he was 'at home, asleep, alone, which is normal'.
There is a single rubber chicken on the floor of the loading area.
Neil once said the chickens were 'worth a fortune to the right people'.
The night guard asked last week what the chickens were insured for.
The loading area door was propped open with a fire extinguisher.

investigations.label: VISIT THE MARKET STALL
investigations.text: The stall holder says a man in a security jumper sold them the lot for forty quid.

investigations.label: CHECK THE CCTV
investigations.text: Camera 4 was facing the wall. It is always facing the wall.

investigations.label: COUNT THE CHICKENS
investigations.text: Forty-one missing, one dropped. Forty sold at the market. The numbers work.

questions.ask: HOW DID THEY GET THEM OUT?

items.reveal: The night guard switched the alarm off, loaded forty-one rubber chickens into his van through the loading area and sold forty of them at the market for forty pounds.
items.graham_reveal: Forty pounds. For our chickens. Insulting.

items.title: WHO WAS WALKING IN STUDIO C?
items.setup: After the 1998 Christmas special, the cleaner heard footsteps crossing Studio C. The studio was locked and empty. The lights were off.

evidence.text: The floor of Studio C was polished that evening. There are no footprints on it.
The heating pipes run under Studio C. They tick and knock as they cool.
The cleaner says the steps 'stopped at the podiums and stood there'.
Pipes don't usually stop at podiums.
The cleaner had worked a double shift and hadn't slept.
In the morning, podium 4's lamp was switched on.
Podium 4's lamp switch is faulty. It sometimes turns itself on.
Nobody will say who stood at podium 4 in the Christmas special.
The building is old and has 'a lot of noises', says Neil, without being asked.

investigations.label: LISTEN TO THE PIPES
investigations.text: When the heating goes off, the pipes knock slowly, about one step a second.

investigations.label: CHECK THE RUNNING ORDER
investigations.text: The 1998 Christmas running order has a contestant 4. The name has been cut out of the page.

investigations.label: ASK THE CLEANER AGAIN
investigations.text: 'It wasn't the pipes. I know the pipes.'

items.reveal: The best-supported answer: the heating pipes cooling, heard by an exhausted cleaner. Nobody has explained podium 4's lamp, or the cut-out name.
items.graham_reveal: Pipes. It was the pipes. Next question.

items.title: WHY DID THE TEA TASTE OF HAIR?
items.setup: On Tuesday, every cup of tea from the staff urn tasted faintly of hair and hairspray. Production stopped for an hour.

evidence.text: Graham arrived on Tuesday 'with a new, more natural look'.
The urn lid was found on the floor. Somebody had looked inside it.
Make-up reports a hairpiece 'went missing from the dressing room for about an hour'.
The urn's water is a strange shiny brown with a film on top.
Graham's dressing room is next to the kitchenette. He 'never uses the kitchenette'.
There is a hairnet hanging on the urn tap.
Neil says it was 'obviously the water supply'.
The hairspray smell is a brand called 'STUDIO HOLD 98'. Only make-up stocks it.
Graham insisted on making his own tea all day 'for reasons'.

investigations.label: DRAIN THE URN
investigations.text: At the bottom: one small, sad, well-steamed hairpiece.

investigations.label: ASK MAKE-UP
investigations.text: 'He came in looking for it in a panic. Then he came back with it wet and said nothing.'

investigations.label: TEST THE WATER SUPPLY
investigations.text: Tap water elsewhere is fine.

items.reveal: Graham dropped his new hairpiece into the urn while trying a 'natural look' between takes, fished it out, and said nothing.
items.graham_reveal: That's not what happened and I won't be answering questions.

items.title: WHAT IS THE SMELL IN THE GREEN ROOM?
items.setup: For three days the Green Room has smelled 'like a warm bin full of fish'. Contestants have complained. Somebody was sick in a plant pot.

evidence.text: The smell is worst near the sofa.
A prawn cocktail went missing from the hospitality tray on Friday.
The sofa cushions unzip. One zip has been opened and closed recently.
The radiator has been stuck on full since Friday.
A contestant on Friday 'didn't eat anything' but had sauce on their sleeve.
The plant pot is a separate, unrelated incident. Allegedly.
There is a faint pink stain on the underside of the middle cushion.
Carol has been spraying perfume 'at it' every morning.
There is a mouse hole behind the sofa, and the mouse has not been seen since Friday.

investigations.label: UNZIP THE CUSHIONS
investigations.text: Inside the middle cushion: a prawn cocktail glass, on its side, very warm.

investigations.label: CHECK BEHIND THE SOFA
investigations.text: The mouse is fine. It's eating crisps. It looks well.

investigations.label: FEEL THE RADIATOR
investigations.text: Scalding. It's been slow-cooking the sofa for three days.

items.reveal: A nervous contestant hid an untouched prawn cocktail inside a sofa cushion on Friday. The radiator has been gently cooking it ever since.
items.graham_reveal: We've burned the sofa. We've kept the mouse.

items.title: WHO MOVED THE TAPES?
items.setup: Every morning this week, the archive tapes have been found re-shelved in a different order. The tape room is locked at night. Only one key exists.

evidence.text: The archivist keeps the only key on a string around her neck. She sleeps with it on.
The new order isn't random: the tapes are now sorted by contestant number.
Every tape featuring podium 4 has been moved to the top shelf.
There's dust on every shelf, but none on the tapes.
The archivist sleepwalks. Her flatmate confirms it.
The archivist lives forty minutes away.
The tape room door has a gap underneath. You could slide something under it. Not a person.
The security guard 'never goes in there'. He says this three times.
One tape has been left playing on the machine: 30 seconds of an empty Studio C.

investigations.label: CHECK THE SIGN-IN SHEET
investigations.text: Nobody has signed in after 7pm all week. The guard's handwriting is on every line.

investigations.label: WATCH THE PLAYING TAPE
investigations.text: Empty Studio C. At 0:28, the podium 4 lamp comes on.

investigations.label: ASK THE ARCHIVIST
investigations.text: 'I don't sleepwalk forty minutes. I'd know.' She looks very tired.

items.reveal: Best supported: someone with access is searching the archive for contestant 4. The guard is the only person who could get in. We don't know that it was him.
items.graham_reveal: Nobody needs those tapes. Nobody watches them. Let's move on.
